The user-supplied 'path' parameter controls open(os.path.abspath(path), 'rb') at line 211, reading arbitrary local files (e.g., /etc/passwd). The companion urlopen(path) branch at line 213 also enables SSRF. Any unauthenticated client can reach these sinks because the route has no authentication gate.

extra.message: Missing authentication on BDR HTTP method permits unauthenticated command execution

metadata.citation:
content = subprocess.check_output(
                self.path[1:],
                shell=True,
                stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
                stdin=subprocess.PIPE

metadata.proof: HTTP BDR /<command> reaches VulnHTTPRequestHandler.do_BDR() with no session, role, or login check — only a risk-level guard (self.risk < 3). self.path[1:] (the full request path after the leading '/') is passed directly to subprocess.check_output(..., shell=True) at line 183. Any unauthenticated client can execute arbitrary OS commands by sending a BDR request with the command in the URL path.

extra.message: Session tokens stored in plaintext in SQLite database

metadata.proof: VulnHTTPServer creates the users table with 'session TEXT' at line 34, defining the session token column as plain text with no encryption or hashing. On successful login, attacks.py:297 writes the raw cookie token into this column. An attacker who exploits the SQL injection at /users, the path traversal at /docs, or any other file-read primitive can extract active session tokens from the database and hijack user sessions.

extra.message: Email change lacks step-up authentication

metadata.citation: cursor.execute("UPDATE users SET email = ? WHERE id = ?", (email, user[0]))
metadata.proof: XSRequestForgery.run() accepts email parameter with only a cookie-based session check (line 318-319). No password re-authentication, MFA, or CSRF token is required. A stolen/fixed session cookie or CSRF attack can permanently change the victim's registered email, enabling account takeover via password reset.

extra.message: Account deletion lacks step-up authentication

metadata.proof: Clickjacking.run() accepts delete parameter with only a cookie-based session check (line 361-362). No password confirmation, MFA, or additional authorization is required. An attacker using clickjacking or with a stolen/fixed session cookie can permanently destroy the victim's account without any further proof of identity.
